info.description:
# Introduction Welcome to the TheirStack API - the largest database of jobs and technographics.
You can use this API to access all our API endpoints, such as the [Jobs endpoint](#tag/jobs/POST/v1/jobs/search) to get real-time and historical jobs from more than 100 countries, the [Companies endpoint](#tag/companies/POST/v1/companies/search) to get a list of companies by the technology they use or by the roles they are hiring for, or the [Technographics endpoint](#tag/companies/POST/v1/companies/technologies) to get a list of technologies used by a company. The API is organized around [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/REST). All requests should be made over SSL. All request and response bodies, including errors, are encoded in JSON. A Swagger UI of these docs is also available at [/openapi](/openapi). --- # Authentication Authentication is done via the API key which you can find in [your account settings](https://app.theirstack.com/settings/api). When making a call, you'll have to specify this API key with the Authorization header. Here's an example: ```sh Authorization: Bearer ``` --- # Pagination Responses that return a list of items are paginated. We offer two different pagination strategies: - **Page-based**: This method allows you to navigate through paginated data by specifying the `page` and `limit` parameters. The `page` parameter indicates the page number you wish to retrieve, while the `limit` parameter specifies the maximum number of items to return per page. For POST requests, include these parameters in the request body. For GET requests, use them as query parameters. - **Offset-based**: This method allows you to navigate through paginated data by specifying the `offset` and `limit` parameters. The `offset` parameter indicates the starting point within the collection of results, while the `limit` parameter specifies the maximum number of items to return. For POST requests, include these parameters in the request body. For GET requests, use them as query parameters. Some of these endpoints also support the `include_total_results` body or query parameter. If you set it to `false`, the responses will be faster, and the field `total_results` of the response will be `null`. --- # Rate Limit All API endpoints are rate limited to ensure reliability and fair usage. When a limit is exceeded, the API returns **HTTP 429 Too Many Requests**. Limits are applied **per user** (or per API key) with sliding windows; multiple windows may apply simultaneously. ## Tiered endpoints and limits Endpoints covered by tier-based limits: * POST `/v1/jobs/search` (Jobs Search) * POST `/v1/companies/search` (Companies Search) * POST `/v1/companies/technologies` (Technographics) Shared limits across all three endpoints: | Tier | API limits | | ---- | ------------------------------------- | | Free | 4/second, 10/minute, 50/hour, 400/day | | Paid | 4/second | - **Paid tier** applies to users who have made at least one payment. - **Free tier** applies to all other users (users who have never paid or users without any payments done). Multiple limits are applied simultaneously. A request is rejected if it exceeds **any** active window. ## Rate limit headers The API returns rate limit information in every response. We follow the **IETF HTTPAPI draft** for RateLimit headers: [RateLimit header fields for HTTP](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/). When multiple rate limits apply, header items are comma-separated and ordered consistently across headers. ### IETF compliant headers - `RateLimit`: Current quota status per policy. Format: `""; r=; t=; pk=`. - `RateLimit-Policy`: Applied policy definition. Format: `""; q=; w=`. ### Other headers These are included for client convenience: - `RateLimit-Limit`: Total allowed requests for each window - `RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining in each window - `RateLimit-Reset`: Seconds until the current window resets The order of values in legacy headers **matches the order of `RateLimit` items**. Example response headers: ``` RateLimit: "per-second";r=3;t=1;pk="dXNlcjoxMjM0", "per-minute";r=9;t=60;pk="dXNlcjoxMjM0", "per-hour";r=49;t=3600;pk="dXNlcjoxMjM0", "per-day";r=399;t=86400;pk="dXNlcjoxMjM0" RateLimit-Policy: "per-second";q=4;w=1, "per-minute";q=10;w=60, "per-hour";q=50;w=3600, "per-day";q=400;w=86400 RateLimit-Limit: 4, 10, 50, 400 RateLimit-Remaining: 3, 9, 49, 399 RateLimit-Reset: 1, 60, 3600, 86400 ``` ## Exceeding limits and best practices * Retry with **exponential backoff** on HTTP 429 responses. * Monitor `RateLimit` or `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` to avoid hitting limits. * Prefer batching and caching to reduce request counts. * Avoid concurrent bursts that violate per-second limits. ---

get.description: Get which optional emails the current user receives, grouped by category (usage, alerts, onboarding): `form_data` holds each preference as `true` or `false`, and `schema` describes each one. get.description: List your team's individual API and app requests in a time range. Each request reports how many credits it consumed (api_credits, ui_credits), its response time (duration, in seconds), HTTP status code, endpoint type and the number of records returned. Use it to inspect per-request consumption and latency. Set group_by=search_pattern to return named summaries in groups, with an empty data list. Search patterns group requests with the same stable filters and includes credits, records, company domain sends and deduplication coverage. The date range selects when requests ran. Filter by types, exact endpoint path, origin, API key or search_pattern_key. Use credit_start_datetime/credit_end_datetime to find requests charged in that window even if they ran earlier; no request-date defaults apply in charge-window mode, and metadata.total_results reports matching requests. Unlinked charges have no request to return. Otherwise defaults to the last 5 days.

Build a deep link into the TheirStack app for a given resource and return it as `{"url": ...}`. Pick the resource with the `type` field: `company_list` (view a list), `job_search` / `company_search` (open a search from the same filters a job or company search takes), `saved_search` (open a saved search), or `webhook` (view a webhook). Search links (`job_search` / `company_search`) are workspace-independent — the encoded query opens against whoever's session loads it, so the link is portable when shared. The other types point at a workspace-specific resource and include the workspace, which is taken from the authenticated caller, so it is never passed in.

List all keywords tracked by TheirStack, including both technologies and buying intent topics. Search for any keyword and filter by one or more categories.

Free: it doesn't consume credits.

- To get technologies only: filter with `keyword_type=technology`
- To get only buying intent topics: filter with `keyword_type_not=technology`

**Building an autocomplete?** The catalog is meant to be queried, not downloaded — there are 42k keywords, so pulling them all is a ~27MB response and should never sit on a user's path:

- On open, with no query: `?limit=50`. Results are sorted by number of companies, so you get the most popular technologies for the empty state. Cache this for hours or a day; it moves slowly.
- As the user types: `?q=snow&limit=10`. This is the search path and ranks the closest matches first.
- Debounce keystrokes by ~200ms so a four-letter query fires one request, not four.

Fetching the full catalog with a large `limit` is only appropriate for an offline, server-side sync — never for a picker.

Response always includes `data` (array of keywords) and `metadata` (total_results, page, limit).

post.description:
Search and filter job postings (job ads, vacancies, hiring data) from thousands of company career sites and job boards. Filter by job title, keywords in the job description, company (name, domain or LinkedIn URL), location and country, technology and tech stack, salary, seniority, remote/hybrid, employment type, and posting date. Used for sales prospecting and lead generation, recruiting, and hiring-trend and market research.

It consumes **1 API credit** for each job returned in the response.

You must specify at least one of the following filters, or otherwise your request will fail: `posted_at_max_age_days`, `posted_at_gte`, `posted_at_lte`, `job_id_or`, `company_domain_or`, `company_linkedin_url_or`, `company_name_or`, `company_name_case_insensitive_or`, `company_name_partial_match_or`. This is for performance reasons.

To get the jobs of specific companies, filter by `company_domain_or` (the identifier we have for the most companies), `company_linkedin_url_or`, `company_name_or` or `company_name_case_insensitive_or`. Company identifier filters are combined with OR: a job matches when its company matches any value in any of them. If you identify companies in more than one way, send a separate request for each company.

Useful resources: [Avoiding getting the same job twice](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/guides/avoid-getting-same-jobs-twice), [Fetching jobs periodically](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/guides/fetch-jobs-periodically), [Preview data mode](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/features/preview-data-mode), [Counting results](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/features/count-results)

job_description_pattern_is_case_insensit.title: Job Description Pattern Is Case Insensitive

job_description_contains_not.title: Job Description Contains Not

Results will exclude jobs whose description contains any of these words.

job_location_pattern_not.title: Job Location Pattern Not

WARNING: Deprecated parameter. closed_at_lte.description: ISO 8601 date string (yyyy-mm-dd). Only return jobs closed on this date or before.

property_exists_or.description: Return jobs that have any of these fields not null. For example, if you pass ['final_url'], it will return jobs that have a final_url set. This field also supports chaining of fields. For example, if you pass ['company_object.domain', 'company_object.linkedin_url'], it will return jobs that have a company domain or a company linkedin_url set.

property_exists_and.title: Property Exists And
property_exists_and.description: Return jobs that have all of these fields not null. For example, if you pass ['company_object.domain', 'final_url'], it will only return jobs that have both a company domain and a final_url set.

company_name_or.title: Company Name Or
company_name_or.description: Only return companies that match these names exactly, case-sensitively. This filter acts as an OR filter, so if you pass more than one company name, it will return companies that match any of the names.

company_name_case_insensitive_or.title: Company Name Case Insensitive Or
company_name_case_insensitive_or.description: Only return companies that match these names exactly, case-insensitively.

company_id_or.title: Company Id Or
company_id_or.description: Only return companies that match these IDs exactly. This filter acts as an OR filter, so if you pass more than one company ID, it will return companies that match any of the IDs.

company_id_not.title: Company Id Not
company_id_not.description: Exclude companies that match these IDs. This filter acts as a NOT filter, so if you pass more than one company ID, it will exclude companies that match any of the IDs.

company_domain_or.title: Company Domain Or
company_domain_or.description: Only return companies that match these domains exactly. It accepts full urls (https://www.google.com/) and emails (andrew@stripe.com). This filter acts as an OR filter, so if you pass more than one company domain, it will return companies that match any of the domains.

company_domain_not.title: Company Domain Not
company_domain_not.description: Only return companies that don't match these domains exactly. It accepts full urls (https://www.google.com/) and emails (andrew@stripe.com).

company_name_not.title: Company Name Not
company_name_not.description: Only return companies that don't match these names exactly, case-sensitively.

company_name_partial_match_or.title: Company Name Partial Match Or
company_name_partial_match_or.description: Company names. Will return companies whose name contains any of the substrings passed here, case-insensitively. For example, if you pass "google", it will return "Google", "Google LLC", "Google Inc", etc.

company_name_partial_match_not.title: Company Name Partial Match Not
company_name_partial_match_not.description: Company names. Will return companies whose name doesn't contain any of the substrings passed here, case-insensitively. For example, if you pass 'google', it will exclude 'Google', 'Google LLC', 'Google Inc', etc.

company_linkedin_url_or.title: Company Linkedin Url Or
company_linkedin_url_or.description: Return companies whose LinkedIn page matches any of the values passed here. Both forms of LinkedIn company URL work — the vanity slug (`https://www.linkedin.com/company/google/`) and the numeric company ID (`https://www.linkedin.com/company/1038`) — as do a bare slug (`google`) and a bare numeric ID (`1038`). A numeric value is matched against the company's LinkedIn ID and its slug, so you do not need to know which of the two you are holding. We have a LinkedIn slug for ~26% of companies and a numeric LinkedIn ID for ~14%, so if you have the company's domain, `company_domain_or` matches more often.

blur_company_data.title: Blur Company Data
blur_company_data.description: Enable preview mode to return blurred data without consuming credits in the TheirStack app. Deprecated: preview mode is being retired and will stop working over the API. It still works on paid workspaces created before August 11, 2026 and is not available on any other workspace; new access is only granted to sales intelligence products that preview data to their end users before unlocking it, by opening a support ticket at https://app.theirstack.com/support/new. When enabled, sensitive company fields (name, domain, URLs, descriptions) and job-specific fields (description, URLs) are blurred. Not available when filtering by company identifiers (company_name, company_domain, company_linkedin_url, company_id). Learn more in the [preview mode documentation](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/features/preview-data-mode).

company_description_pattern_or.title: Company Description Pattern Or
company_description_pattern_or.description: Case-insensitive patterns to match in the company description. Will return companies that match any of the patterns.

company_description_pattern_not.title: Company Description Pattern Not
company_description_pattern_not.description: Case-insensitive patterns to match in the company description. Will exclude companies that match any of the patterns.

company_description_pattern_accent_insen.title: Company Description Pattern Accent Insensitive
company_description_pattern_accent_insen.description: Set to True to make company description searches accent insensitive. For example, "á" will match "a" as well.

min_employee_count.title: Min Employee Count
min_employee_count.description: Minimum number of employees in a company

max_employee_count.title: Max Employee Count
max_employee_count.description: Maximum number of employees in a company

min_employee_count_or_null.title: Min Employee Count Or Null
min_employee_count_or_null.description: Minimum number of employees in a company. If we don't have company size information, we will return it as well.

max_employee_count_or_null.title: Max Employee Count Or Null
max_employee_count_or_null.description: Maximum number of employees in a company. If we don't have company size information, we will return it as well.

funding_stage_or.title: Funding Stage Or
funding_stage_or.description: Funding stages of companies returned. Possible values: ['angel', 'convertible_note', 'debt_financing', 'equity_crowdfunding', 'other', 'private_equity', 'seed', 'series_a', 'series_b', 'series_c', 'series_d', 'series_e', 'series_f', 'series_g', 'series_h', 'venture_round_not_specified', 'series_i', 'series_j', 'undisclosed', 'series_unknown', 'pre_seed', 'post_ipo_secondary', 'post_ipo_equity', 'post_ipo_debt', 'non_equity_assistance', 'late_vc', 'initial_coin_offering', 'growth_equity_vc', 'grant', 'early_vc', 'corporate_round', 'secondary_market', 'product_crowdfunding']

industry_or.title: Industry Or
industry_or.description:
Names of industries, case-insensitive. Results will only include companies that belong to any of the industries specified in this parameter. Available values: [GET /v0/catalog/industries](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_industries_v0)

    WARNING: Deprecated parameter. Use the industry_id_or field instead.

industry_not.title: Industry Not
industry_not.description:
Names of industries, case-insensitive. Results will exclude companies that belong to any of the industries specified in this parameter. Available values: [GET /v0/catalog/industries](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_industries_v0)

    WARNING: Deprecated parameter. Use the industry_id_not field instead.

industry_id_or.title: Industry Id Or
industry_id_or.description: Industry codes. You can use any of [LinkedIn's Industry Codes V2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/references/reference-tables/industry-codes-v2) or [GET /v0/catalog/industries](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_industries_v0)

industry_id_not.title: Industry Id Not
industry_id_not.description: Industry ids to exclude. You can use any of [LinkedIn's Industry Codes V2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/references/reference-tables/industry-codes-v2) or [GET /v0/catalog/industries](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_industries_v0)

industry_id_not_or_null.title: Industry Id Not Or Null
industry_id_not_or_null.description: Industry ids to exclude. Companies whose industry we don't know are returned as well. You can use any of [LinkedIn's Industry Codes V2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/references/reference-tables/industry-codes-v2) or [GET /v0/catalog/industries](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_industries_v0)

company_tags_or.title: Company Tags Or
company_tags_or.description: Return companies that match any of these keywords

company_investors_partial_match_or.title: Company Investors Partial Match Or
company_investors_partial_match_or.description: Investors of the company. Will return companies for which any of their investors contains any of the substrings passed here. For example, if you pass 'andree', all funds that match it (like 'Andreessen Horowitz', 'Andreessen Horowitz LLC', etc).

company_technology_slug_or.title: Company Technology Slug Or
company_technology_slug_or.description: Return results from companies that have mentioned any of these technologies in their jobs (in job searches, not necessarily in the jobs returned). Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`

company_technology_slug_and.title: Company Technology Slug And
company_technology_slug_and.description: Return results from companies that have mentioned all of these technologies in their jobs (in job searches, not necessarily in the jobs returned). Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`

company_technology_slug_not.title: Company Technology Slug Not
company_technology_slug_not.description: Return results from companies that haven't mentioned any of these technologies in their jobs. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`

company_keyword_slug_or.title: Company Keyword Slug Or
company_keyword_slug_or.description: Return results from companies that have mentioned any of these keywords in their jobs. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

company_keyword_slug_and.title: Company Keyword Slug And
company_keyword_slug_and.description: Return results from companies that have mentioned all of these keywords in their jobs. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

company_keyword_slug_not.title: Company Keyword Slug Not
company_keyword_slug_not.description: Return results from companies that haven't mentioned any of these keywords in their jobs. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

company_location_pattern_or.title: Company Location Pattern Or
company_location_pattern_or.description: Return companies whose city matches any of the patterns passed here. Case insensitive. For example, if you pass 'san francisco', it will return companies whose city is 'San Francisco', 'San Francisco Bay Area', etc.

company_country_code_or.title: Company Country Code Or
company_country_code_or.description: Return companies whose HQ country code is any of the ones passed here, case sensitive. Pass ISO2 country codes.

company_country_code_not.title: Company Country Code Not
company_country_code_not.description: Return companies whose HQ country code is not any of the ones passed here, case sensitive. Pass ISO2 country codes.

company_country_code_not_or_null.title: Company Country Code Not Or Null
company_country_code_not_or_null.description: Return companies whose HQ country code is not any of the ones passed here, case sensitive. Companies whose country we don't know are returned as well. Pass ISO2 country codes.

company_list_id_or.title: Company List Id Or
company_list_id_or.description: Return companies that belong to any of the company lists passed here

company_list_id_not.title: Company List Id Not
company_list_id_not.description: Return companies that don't belong to any of the company lists passed here

company_linkedin_url_exists.title: Company Linkedin Url Exists
company_linkedin_url_exists.description: (Use `property_exists_or / property_exists_and` instead) Only return companies with a LinkedIn URL

revealed_company_data.title: Revealed Company Data
revealed_company_data.description: Filter companies (or jobs by their company) by whether the caller's team has them revealed. A company counts as revealed for 90 days after the team reveals it. `true` returns only revealed companies; `false` returns only companies the team has not revealed in the last 90 days, including the ones it never revealed.

company_revealed_at_gte.title: Company Revealed At Gte
company_revealed_at_gte.description: Filter companies (or jobs by their company) by when the company was revealed in the caller's account. Returns only companies revealed at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Scoped to the caller's team — has no effect for companies the team has never revealed.

company_revealed_at_lte.title: Company Revealed At Lte
company_revealed_at_lte.description: Filter companies (or jobs by their company) by when the company was revealed in the caller's account. Returns only companies revealed at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp. Scoped to the caller's team — has no effect for companies the team has never revealed.

company_not_revealed_at_gte.title: Company Not Revealed At Gte
company_not_revealed_at_gte.description: Exclude companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Combine with `company_not_revealed_at_lte` to exclude a window. Companies the team never revealed are kept.

company_not_revealed_at_lte.title: Company Not Revealed At Lte
company_not_revealed_at_lte.description: Exclude companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp. Combine with `company_not_revealed_at_gte` to exclude a window. Companies the team never revealed are kept.

company_revealed_within_hours.title: Company Revealed Within Hours
company_revealed_within_hours.description: Return only companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account in the last N hours, counted back from when the search runs. `168` is the last 7 days. Saved searches and webhooks resolve the window on every run. It counts every reveal in the window: with N above 90 days (2160 hours) it also returns companies whose 90-day reveal has expired, which cost a credit to see again.

company_not_revealed_within_hours.title: Company Not Revealed Within Hours
company_not_revealed_within_hours.description: Exclude companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account in the last N hours, counted back from when the search runs. `168` hides what the team revealed in the last 7 days; companies revealed earlier, or never, are kept. Viewing an already-revealed company again does not restart its window. Unlike `revealed_company_data=false`, which excludes the whole 90-day reveal period, this only excludes reveals inside the window.

last_funding_round_date_lte.title: Last Funding Round Date Lte
last_funding_round_date_lte.description: Only return companies whose last funding round date is before or on this date. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'

last_funding_round_date_gte.title: Last Funding Round Date Gte
last_funding_round_date_gte.description: Only return companies whose last funding round date is after or on this date. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD'

include_total_results.title: Include Total Results
include_total_results.description: When enabled, calculates and returns `total_results` and `total_companies` fields in the response. WARNING: This significantly slows down responses as it requires reading the entire dataset. Recommended usage: enable only for the initial request to get totals, then disable for subsequent pagination requests.

order_by.title: Order By
order_by.description: List of column objects. You can pass several columns to order by, in order of priority. Only `field` is required, `desc` is True by default.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Number of results to skip. Required for [offset-based pagination](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/pagination).

job_title_or.title: Job Title Or
job_title_or.description: Keyword-based patterns to match job titles. Case-insensitive. Returns jobs whose title contains all the words in any of the patterns, in any order. For example, `marketing vp` matches titles such as `VP of Marketing` or `Marketing VP, EMEA`. Passing `["software engineer", "data scientist"]` returns jobs matching either pattern.

job_title_not.title: Job Title Not
job_title_not.description: Keyword-based patterns to exclude job titles. Case-insensitive. Excludes jobs whose title contains all the words in any of the patterns, in any order. For example, `marketing vp` excludes titles such as `VP of Marketing` or `Marketing VP, EMEA`.

job_title_pattern_and.title: Job Title Pattern And
job_title_pattern_and.description: Regex patterns to match job titles. Case-insensitive. Only jobs with title that match all of these patterns will be returned.

job_title_pattern_or.title: Job Title Pattern Or
job_title_pattern_or.description: Regex patterns to match job titles. Case-insensitive. Jobs whose job title matches any of the patterns will be returned.

job_title_pattern_not.title: Job Title Pattern Not
job_title_pattern_not.description: Regex patterns to match job titles. Case-insensitive. Jobs whose job title doesn't match any of the patterns will be returned.

job_country_code_or.title: Job Country Code Or
job_country_code_or.description: 2-letter ISO country code of the location of the job. Can pass more than 1

job_country_code_not.title: Job Country Code Not
job_country_code_not.description: 2-letter ISO country code of the location of the job. Can pass more than 1. Will exclude jobs from these countries

posted_at_max_age_days.title: Posted At Max Age Days
posted_at_max_age_days.description: Date posted max age in days. If 0, only return jobs posted today. If 1, from today and yesterday, etc.

posted_at_gte.title: Posted At Gte
posted_at_gte.description: ISO 8601 date string (yyyy-mm-dd). Only jobs published in this date or after will be returned.

posted_at_lte.title: Posted At Lte
posted_at_lte.description: ISO 8601 date string (yyyy-mm-dd). Only jobs published in this date or before will be returned.

discovered_at_max_age_days.title: Discovered At Max Age Days
discovered_at_max_age_days.description: If 0, only return jobs added to our database in the current day. If 1, from today and yesterday, etc.

discovered_at_min_age_days.title: Discovered At Min Age Days
discovered_at_min_age_days.description: If 1, only return jobs discovered by TheirStack until yesterday. If 2, until 2 days ago, etc.

discovered_at_gte.title: Discovered At Gte
discovered_at_gte.description: Only jobs discovered by TheirStack on this date or datetime or after will be returned. In UTC timezone.

discovered_at_lte.title: Discovered At Lte
discovered_at_lte.description: Only jobs discovered by TheirStack on this date or datetime or before will be returned. In UTC timezone.

job_description_pattern_or.title: Job Description Pattern Or
job_description_pattern_or.description: Regex patterns to look for in job descriptions. Case-sensitive. Results will include jobs whose description matches any of these patterns. Use (?i) at the start of a pattern to make it case-insensitive. Can pass more than one.

job_description_pattern_not.title: Job Description Pattern Not
job_description_pattern_not.description: Regex patterns to look for in job descriptions. Case-sensitive. Results will include jobs whose description doesn't match any of these patterns. Use (?i) at the start of a pattern to make it case-insensitive. Can pass more than one.

job_description_pattern_and.title: Job Description Pattern And
job_description_pattern_and.description: Regex patterns that must ALL match the job description (AND logic). Use (?i) at the start of a pattern to make it case-insensitive. Results will only include jobs whose description matches every pattern in this list.

job_description_pattern_is_case_insensit.title: Job Description Pattern Is Case Insensitive

job_description_contains_or.title: Job Description Contains Or
job_description_contains_or.description: Search for whole words in job descriptions using word boundaries (\b). Case-insensitive by default, except for the patterns that are uppercase - in that case we'll respect it. Only finds complete words (e.g., searching 'quality' won't match 'inequality'). Results will include jobs whose description contains any of these words.

job_description_contains_not.title: Job Description Contains Not
job_description_contains_not.description: Exclude jobs whose description contains any of these whole words using word boundaries (\b). Case-insensitive by default, except for the patterns that are uppercase - in that case we'll respect it. Only finds complete words (e.g., searching 'quality' won't match 'inequality'). Results will exclude jobs whose description contains any of these words.

job_description_pattern_case_sensitive_o.title: Job Description Pattern Case Sensitive Or
job_description_pattern_case_sensitive_o.description: Deprecated. Use job_description_pattern_or instead, which now behaves identically.

remote.title: Remote
remote.description: Deprecated. Use workplace_types_or instead. True: only show remote jobs. False: only show non-remote jobs. None: show all jobs.

workplace_types_or.title: Workplace Types Or
workplace_types_or.description: Filter jobs by workplace type. Returns jobs that match any of the specified workplace types. `on_site` matches jobs that are neither hybrid nor remote. If no values are provided or an empty list is sent, jobs are not filtered by workplace type.

only_jobs_with_reports_to.title: Only Jobs With Reports To
only_jobs_with_reports_to.description: Only return jobs where we identified the role the hired person would report to. Deprecated field, use reports_to_exists instead.

reports_to_exists.title: Reports To Exists
reports_to_exists.description: Only return jobs where we identified the role the hired person would report to. If True, only return jobs where we identified the role the hired person would report to. If False, only return jobs where we didn't identify the role the hired person would report to. If None, return all jobs.

final_url_exists.title: Final Url Exists
final_url_exists.description: (Use `property_exists_or / property_exists_and` instead) Only return jobs with a final URL. Typically jobs that were originally posted on an ATS. If True, only return jobs with a final URL. If False, only return jobs without a final URL. If None, return all jobs.

only_jobs_with_hiring_managers.title: Only Jobs With Hiring Managers
only_jobs_with_hiring_managers.description: Only return jobs with a hiring manager. If True, only return jobs with a hiring manager. If False, only return jobs without a hiring manager. If None, return all jobs.

hiring_managers_exists.title: Hiring Managers Exists
hiring_managers_exists.description: (Use `property_exists_or / property_exists_and` instead) If True, only return jobs with a hiring manager. If False, only return jobs without a hiring manager. If None, return all jobs.

job_id_or.title: Job Id Or
job_id_or.description: Get jobs with these IDs only.

job_ids.title: Job Ids
job_ids.description: Get jobs with these IDs only. Deprecated parameter, use job_id_or instead.

job_seniority_or.title: Job Seniority Or
job_seniority_or.description: Will return jobs where the seniority is any of the ones passed here

min_salary_usd.title: Min Salary Usd
min_salary_usd.description: Minimum annual salary in USD. For example, 100000 means $100,000.

max_salary_usd.title: Max Salary Usd
max_salary_usd.description: Maximum annual salary in USD. For example, 150000 means $150,000.

job_technology_slug_or.title: Job Technology Slug Or
job_technology_slug_or.description: Will return jobs where any of these technologies appear. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`. If you pass more than one technology, we will return jobs that mention at least one of them.

job_technology_slug_not.title: Job Technology Slug Not
job_technology_slug_not.description: Will return jobs where none of these technologies appear. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`.

job_technology_slug_and.title: Job Technology Slug And
job_technology_slug_and.description: Will return jobs where all of these technologies appear. Case sensitive. Pass slugs. Check out all the technologies we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0) with `keyword_type=technology`.

job_keyword_slug_or.title: Job Keyword Slug Or
job_keyword_slug_or.description: Will return jobs where any of these keyword slugs appear. Case sensitive. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

job_keyword_slug_and.title: Job Keyword Slug And
job_keyword_slug_and.description: Will return jobs where all of these keyword slugs appear. Case sensitive. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

job_keyword_slug_not.title: Job Keyword Slug Not
job_keyword_slug_not.description: Will return jobs where none of these keyword slugs appear. Case sensitive. Check out all the keywords we track at [GET /v0/catalog/keywords](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_keywords_v0)

job_location_pattern_or.title: Job Location Pattern Or
job_location_pattern_or.description:
Regex patterns to match job locations. Case-insensitive. Searches both the location field and the enhanced locations array (using normalized city and state name fields within each location element). Jobs matching ANY of the provided patterns will be returned.

WARNING: Deprecated parameter. Use the `job_location_or` filter instead — it uses structured location IDs from the [locations catalog](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_locations_v0), which is more precise, supports hierarchical (country/region/city) and multi-language searches, has fewer false positives, and benefits from indexed lookups and recent accuracy fixes.

job_location_pattern_not.title: Job Location Pattern Not
job_location_pattern_not.description:
Regex patterns to exclude job locations. Case-insensitive. Searches both the location field and the enhanced locations array (using normalized city and state name fields within each location element). Jobs matching ANY of the provided patterns will be EXCLUDED from results.

WARNING: Deprecated parameter. Use the `job_location_not` filter instead — it uses structured location IDs from the [locations catalog](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_locations_v0), which is more precise, supports hierarchical (country/region/city) and multi-language searches, has fewer false positives, and benefits from indexed lookups and recent accuracy fixes.

job_location_or.title: Job Location Or
job_location_or.description: Filter jobs by location. Returns jobs whose locations match ANY of the specified location criteria. Each location criteria is specified using a JobLocationFilter object. (You can find location IDs using the [locations catalog endpoint](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_locations_v0))

job_location_not.title: Job Location Not
job_location_not.description: Filter jobs by location. Returns jobs whose locations DO NOT match ANY of the specified location criteria. Each location criteria is specified using a JobLocationFilter object. (You can find location IDs using the [locations catalog endpoint](https://theirstack.com/en/docs/api-reference/catalog/get_catalog_locations_v0))

url_domain_or.title: Url Domain Or
url_domain_or.description: Include jobs only if their URL domain (from `url` or `source_url`) is in the provided case-insensitive list. For example, ['greenhouse.io', 'workable.com'] will match URLs containing 'greenhouse.io' or 'workable.com'. Refer to our list of sources at https://theirstack.com/en/docs/data/job/sources.

url_domain_not.title: Url Domain Not
url_domain_not.description: Exclude jobs if their URL domain (from `url` or `source_url`) is in the provided case-insensitive list. For example, ['greenhouse.io', 'workable.com'] will exclude URLs containing 'greenhouse.io' or 'workable.com'. Refer to our list of sources at https://theirstack.com/en/docs/data/job/sources.

scraper_name_pattern_or.title: Scraper Name Pattern Or
scraper_name_pattern_or.description: Regex patterns to match job sources. Case-insensitive.

easy_apply.title: Easy Apply
easy_apply.description: If True, only return jobs that can be applied directly through the job board. If False, only return jobs that require redirecting to the company's website.

employment_statuses_or.title: Employment Statuses Or
employment_statuses_or.description: Filter jobs by employment status. Returns jobs that match any of the specified employment types. If no values are provided or an empty list is sent, all jobs regardless of employment status will be returned.

is_closed.title: Is Closed

company_not_revealed_at_gte.title: Company Not Revealed At Gte

company_not_revealed_at_lte.title: Company Not Revealed At Lte
company_not_revealed_at_lte.description: Exclude companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp. Combine with `company_not_revealed_at_gte` to exclude a window. Companies the team never revealed are kept.

company_revealed_within_hours.title: Company Revealed Within Hours

Saved searches and webhooks resolve the window on every run. It counts every reveal in the window: with N above 90 days (2160 hours) it also returns companies whose 90-day reveal has expired, which cost a credit to see again.

company_not_revealed_within_hours.title: Company Not Revealed Within Hours
company_not_revealed_within_hours.description: Exclude companies (or jobs by their company) revealed in the caller's account in the last N hours, counted back from when the search runs. `168` hides what the team revealed in the last 7 days; companies revealed earlier, or never, are kept. Viewing an already-revealed company again does not restart its window. Unlike `revealed_company_data=false`, which excludes the whole 90-day reveal period, this only excludes reveals inside the window.

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer with 5+ years of experience in data engineering to join our growing data team. You will be responsible for designing and implementing scalable data pipelines, data models, and data warehouses that support our business intelligence and analytics initiatives.

- Design, build, and maintain robust, scalable data pipelines using modern data engineering tools and frameworks
- Develop and optimize data models and schemas for data warehouses and data lakes
- Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, and product teams to understand data requirements and deliver solutions

- Optimize query performance and data processing workflows for large-scale datasets
- Build and maintain ETL/ELT processes using tools like Apache Airflow, dbt, or similar
- Work with cloud data platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and their native data services
- Establish data governance practices and ensure compliance with data privacy regulations
- Mentor junior data engineers and contribute to technical documentation

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field
- 5+ years of experience in data engineering or related roles
- Strong proficiency in Python and SQL

- Knowledge of data modeling concepts and best practices
- Experience with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD pipelines
- Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail

## Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with real-time data processing and streaming analytics
- Knowledge of data visualization tools (Tableau, Looker, PowerBI)
- Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)
- Familiarity with machine learning workflows and MLOps practices
- Experience with data governance and cataloging tools

## What We Offer
- Competitive salary and equity package
- Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
- Flexible work arrangements and remote-friendly culture
- Professional development budget for conferences and training
- State-of-the-art equipment and technology stack
- Collaborative and inclusive work environment
- Opportunity to work with cutting-edge data technologies

## What We Offer

True: the feed starts from the moment the webhook is enabled, so records matched while it was disabled are never sent nor charged. Ignored when disabling.

webhook_id.title: Webhook Id
webhook_id.description: ID of an existing webhook to test. When provided, url and event_type are loaded from the stored webhook. Body fields (url, secret) can override stored values.

url.title: Url
url.description: URL to send the test event to. Required when webhook_id is not provided.

event_type.description: Type of event to simulate. Required when webhook_id is not provided.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Secret used to sign webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256. If set, deliveries include an X-TheirStack-Signature-256 header.

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: ID of the search that the webhook is listening to.

listening_start_time.title: Listening Start Time
listening_start_time.description: Date when the webhook started listening for events. If listening_start_time is None, the webhook will listen to all events matching the search query regardless of when they occurred.

trigger_once_per_company.title: Trigger Once Per Company
trigger_once_per_company.description: Only for webhook type ='job.new'. If true, Company A with 5 jobs → 1 event triggered. If false, Company A with 5 jobs → 5 events triggered

active_event_types.title: Active Event Types
active_event_types.description: Event types this webhook subscribes to. If None, defaults to the search type's primary event (job_new for jobs, company_new for companies).

max_events_per_day.title: Max Events Per Day
max_events_per_day.description: Most events sent per UTC day, or null for no cap. Matches over it are dropped, never sent, charged or queued for the next day. Minimum 1: to send nothing, disable the webhook.

secret.title: Secret
secret.description: Secret used to sign webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256. If set, deliveries include an X-TheirStack-Signature-256 header. Omit to keep current value; set to null to remove.

webhook_id.title: Webhook Id
webhook_id.description: ID of the webhook to open

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The saved search this estimate is for.

records_last_7_days.title: Records Last 7 Days
records_last_7_days.description: Records matching the search that we discovered in the last 7 days. When the search's own date filters reach back fewer days (e.g. posted in the last 24 hours), it is measured over that shorter window and scaled to 7 days. Null when the estimate is unavailable.

avg_records_per_day.title: Avg Records Per Day
avg_records_per_day.description: records_last_7_days / 7, rounded down. The number to compare a daily cap against. Null when the estimate is unavailable.

credits_per_record.title: Credits Per Record
credits_per_record.description: API credits one event costs: 1 for jobs, 3 for companies.

avg_credits_per_day.title: Avg Credits Per Day
avg_credits_per_day.description: avg_records_per_day * credits_per_record. Null when the estimate is unavailable.

unavailable_reason.title: Unavailable Reason
unavailable_reason.description: Why there is no estimate, when there is none. Null when there is.

WebhookVolumeEstimate.title: WebhookVolumeEstimate
WebhookVolumeEstimate.description:
What a saved search would send through a webhook on an average day.

Measured from the last 7 days of matches, which is the same number the
scanning-frequency tier is chosen from — one estimate, one meaning, so a
cap warning can never contradict the cadence the webhook actually gets.

The estimate is **null, not zero**, whenever it cannot be measured. Zero is
an answer ("this search matches nothing"); null says we have no number, and
the two must not be confused by anything sizing a cap against it.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: The endpoints in this section let you search for companies with multiple filters, as well as getting technographics info about companies.

tags.name: Saved Searches
tags.description: Saved searches let you save a search query so you can reuse it later. You can save a search by clicking on the 'Save' button on the top of the search results page on app.theirstack.com. You can also create and retrieve saved searches programmatically using this API.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: Catalog with the unique values that you can pass to some filters, such as technologies, industries...

tags.name: Datasets
tags.description: Datasets are a way to get data from TheirStack. We publish datasets of companies, jobs, and technographics, available via S3 as flat files. If you're interested in accessing our data this way, contact us at hi@theirstack.com.

tags.name: Company Lists
tags.description: Company lists are a collection of company identifiers. Currently we use company names as identifiers. Company Lists can be used in other endpoints, such as the job search endpoint or the company search endpoint, to get results only from companies that are or aren't included in one or several lists.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications when events occur (new jobs, new companies) that match your saved search criteria. Configure webhooks to trigger actions in external systems like Zapier, Make, N8N, or your own applications.
